newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait military, officials meet to discuss Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait military, officials meet to discuss Iraq.

text.p: Senior Kuwaiti officials and military officers met on Thursday to discuss growing tension over Iraq as U.S. stealth fighters headed to the Gulf Arab state to be in closer striking range of its northern neighbour.
"Several ministers, senior officers and members of the Supreme Defence Council all attended the meeting," a source close to the government told Reuters.

They discussed "plans and preparations on all sectors of the military...and also reviewed the political contacts with friendly and brotherly states and accords signed with them...An official statement will be issued shortly," the source said.
Kuwait has defence agreements with the United States and the other four permanent members of the United Nations Security Council -- Britain, China, France and Russia.
Several regional states said they had not received any requests from the United States for the use of air bases but some indicated they would have turned them down anyway.

Eight U.S. F-117A stealth fighters flew to Kuwait from the United States and four B-52s moved from Guam in the Pacific Ocean to a British base on the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia to be in closer range of Iraq.

Diplomats and officials were unable immediately to confirm whether the stealth fighters had already arrived in Kuwait, which was liberated by a U.S.-led coalition from Iraqi occupation troops in the 1991 Gulf War.
The latest U.S. military deployment was triggered on Wednesday by Iraq's firing of a surface-to-air missile which missed U.S. warplanes patrolling over northern Iraq.

Last week, in a move which failed to receive backing from Arab allies, the United States fired 44 missiles at Iraqi air defence targets in two raids on southern Iraq in retaliation for its role in factional Kurdish fighting in the north of the country.
